stage_a.note: F1 demonstrates highly positive expression with a bright smile and energetic delivery while dressed as an elf.
F1 shows sustained, pronounced excitement about the venture throughout the pitch, speaking loudly and dynamically.
F1 is very friendly and approachable, maintaining a considerate and welcoming orientation toward the panel.

venture.description: Clip-in ornaments, lights, and glitter designed for decorating facial hair during the holidays.
venture.note: The presenting founder is Jason; the helpers do not hold equity or present the business model.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 introduces himself and the helpers, states the ask, and begins the story of Santa growing bored with his outfit.

turns.speaker: F3
turns.summary: F3 complains that ugly sweaters just looked weird.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 suggests putting stuff in Santa's beard.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains that Santa clipped bright ornaments into his beard, bringing unprecedented holiday spirit.

turns.speaker: F3
turns.summary: F3 excitedly announces the name Beardaments.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 states they can be clipped anywhere, and that Santa knew there must be other ways to deck a beard out.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 explains the elves quickly made beard oil, glitter, and lights.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 says anyone without a Rudolph can see through the night, inviting the sharks to season up their beards.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 asks the sharks to make his Christmas wish come true.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 concludes by telling the sharks to watch their money grow.

turns.speaker: F3
turns.summary: F3 laughs a traditional Santa laugh.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 laughs at the conclusion of the pitch.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 announces that Santa and the Elf will pass out samples to the panel.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 remarks that she thinks she has seen it all.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 agrees with S1's amused remark.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 expresses excitement to put the product on and asks S3 about hers.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 playfully teases S4 that the beard is not his best look.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 reacts to wearing the decorated beard.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 points out that they brought a wig for S2.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 accepts the wig and thanks F1.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 tells S2 that the ornaments can be clipped anywhere.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 thanks F2 for the advice.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 comments that he thinks the wig will look terrific on S2.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 dismisses the helpers so they can leave the stage.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 asks F1 why he came up with this idea.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains he started it four years ago for a party, sold out a thousand packs, and did 80k.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks what sales F1 achieved in his second year.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 states he did 155,000 in sales in his second year.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 asks what sales F1 achieved in the previous year.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 answers 462,000 in sales last year and projects 600-700k for the current year.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 asks if all sales are direct to the consumer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 confirms that all sales are direct to the customer.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 expresses utter disbelief and amazement at the sales figures.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 volunteers the pricing and manufacturing cost for the regular beard ornaments.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 asks what F1 charges for the light-up ornaments.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 states the price and cost for the light-up ornaments.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 asks how long the lights last.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 answers that they last about two days of continuous usage.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 suggests F1 wants the lights to burn out so customers buy again.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 points out people rarely save inexpensive items, implying the short battery life is acceptable.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks how F1 is acquiring customers given the niche target audience.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 attributes success to viral videos with 130 million views, resulting in zero marketing costs.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 challenges whether F1 can achieve that level of viral marketing every year.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 admits he cannot, but explains he maintained sales using email blasts to existing customers.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 asks F1 about his professional background.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains he is a director of sales for a telecom distributor and bootstrapped the business from his basement.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 enthusiastically repeats F1's idea about sports licensing.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 adds an example of using the Mavericks logo.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains his ideas for expanding into sports licensing by selling at stadiums.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 expresses doubt that sports licensing is a great idea.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 asks F1 what he intends to use the investment money for.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 lists four uses: licensing, expanding to other holidays, entering retail, and international expansion.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 praises F1's success but states the business is not investable for him, declaring he is out.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 congratulates F1 on his achievement but agrees he does not need a shark, and exits.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 argues he wants a partner to help scale the business from half a million to several million.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks F1 to justify the 1.5 million dollar valuation.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 justifies the valuation by projecting 250-300k in net profit, making it a 5x multiple.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 cautions against creating new markets for one-product hits, sees no room for partners, and exits.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 thanks S1 for the feedback.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 praises the brand but exits because he wants an entrepreneur who is committed full-time.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 thanks S4.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 asks F1 how he would get his money back if he invested.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 replies S2 would get it back through distributions and by figuring out how to grow sales.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 notes he is the only shark who has made money selling similar unconventional novelty products.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 makes a joking reference to drawing a cat.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 jokingly calls F1 the Tipsy Elf.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 concedes the joke and laughs it off.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 compares the business to his successful Potato Parcel deal, though notes his lack of hair.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 playfully puts the decorated wig on his own head to show S2.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 laughs at F1 wearing the wig.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 remarks that it is one of those specific types of deals.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 offers 150,000 for 25%.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 immediately accepts S2's offer.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 reacts with surprise to the accepted deal.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 shakes hands with F1 and expresses enthusiasm.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 thanks S2 as they finalize the handshake.

decisions.note: F1 is crushing it, doesn't need the sharks, and it's not investable for S5.
Agrees with Mark, thinks F1 has his own business going and doesn't need a shark.
Believes it's a mistake to try to create new markets for a one-product hit, sees no room for partners.
Thinks it's a great part-time gig but wants an entrepreneur who is all in.
Notes he has made money on similar crazy novelty items and finds it tempting.
